precepts.text: I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64: scattered and serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted. James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that had been living as sinners. So count it joy when God starts showing you who you are.
precepts.point: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures. The literal firstfruits brought to God had to be without spot. We are supposed to keep ourselves unspotted from the world; and to become unspotted, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous. The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect; an animal could not be spotted. And James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” But we all fall short.

So who is James writing to? “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

precepts.text: My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew. When Job spoke it was like that; and that right there is prophetic, it is going to come again in the future.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.” They waited for his words with their mouths open. When he was teaching or giving counsel, he was dropping blessings on them, dropping understanding.

It says the same thing as the song of Moses: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”.

So when Job spoke, it was like that: “my speech dropped upon them.” And that right there is prophetic. It is going to come again in the future, near to come.

precepts.text: How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight? Unity. Through us together, unified in Christ, hence the name Israel United in Christ, we can move mountains. Some others do not aspire to do anything; they are fine doing videos from their garages. But the vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you do not have worldwide aspirations, you are not going to do worldwide things; if you think small, you will stay small.
precepts.point: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity. Why is that good and pleasant? Because we cannot be stopped when we are unified.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Why is that good and pleasant? It's the only way we grow, keeping the commandments together as a unit; without unity there is disorder, and nothing gets built. But the reason it is so important is that we can't be stopped when we are unified. Moses shows it: “How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight”?

Unity. That's how we are going to do it: through us together, unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. We can move mountains. It's that type of unity we have to come to and understand, because without it, brothers, we won't do nothing.

Look at some of the others, not doing anything. They don't aspire to do anything; they're fine just where they're at, cool just being in the house, and they will keep doing videos from their garages. But we have worldwide goals. The vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you don't have worldwide aspirations, you're not going to do worldwide things. If you think small, you'll stay small. Shoot for the stars.

The sixty-man camp of 2013 showed it: that small number organized and unified set a standard in the nation, and today one phone call could bring a thousand men. That is one chasing a thousand and two putting ten thousand to flight, when brethren dwell together in unity.

precepts.text: I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. The remembrance of who we are has ceased from amongst men. We didn't just forget; the nations made war with us and used crafty counsel: make sure them slaves cannot read and write. Ask a man today who the Israelites are and he points at the synagogue of Satan. Yet in Africa today there are millions professing they are the Israelites; just in Nigeria there is an Israelite community of millions, and they always knew.
precepts.point: The curses shall be upon thee for a sign, and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. Why a sign? Like a McDonald's sign lets you know a McDonald's is there. Because according to prophecy we would be scattered in slavery and forget our nationality, God said: these curses are going to follow you and your seed, so no matter where you are scattered, when you read the Bible you're going to say, wait, this is talking about my people. In the future, Judah will need to identify who Israel is; today you identify the Israelites by the curses.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” Why a sign? When you see a McDonald's sign, it lets you know a McDonald's is there. The curses have to be upon us for a sign because we would be cut off from our heritage, and in the future Judah will need to identify who Israel is. How do you identify the Israelites today? By the curses.

Deuteronomy 32:26 shows why: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. We were scattered into corners in slavery, and the remembrance of who we are, our nationality, all of it, has ceased from among men. We did not just forget because time went on. We forgot because the nations made war with us and took crafty counsel: make sure those slaves cannot read and write. They destroyed us as a people and took our nationality. Ask a Chinese man today who the Israelites are, and he points at the fake people in the land, the synagogue of Satan.

Yet go to Africa today and you will see millions of people professing that they are the people of God, the Israelites, though you will not see it on the news. Just in Nigeria there is a large Israelite community of millions. Over generations of misinterpretation and mixing customs with the Hamitic tribes they do not keep the laws the way they are supposed to, but they always knew they were Israel.

So God did it real nice. Esau would take our nationality from us, but the curses would follow us and our seed, so that no matter where we are scattered, in Africa, America, South America, China, Iran, the islands, when we read the Bible we say: wait, this is talking about my people.

precepts.text: They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to new gods that came newly up. The white Jesus is a new god, created during the Renaissance. Islam is a new god, created around 600 AD after Christ. Those are the new gods our people went after.
precepts.point: For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. When he comes it is going to be like lightning; he is not going to be in any secret chambers.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
With the technology Esau has, just imagine a white Jesus coming out of the sky in the middle of war, making all the armies of the world put down their weapons, ending war. The elect are not going to believe it, and we are going to be enemy number one. Why? Because we know the scriptures. Christ already warned us: “believe it not.” It might be possible to deceive some, but not the elect.

“They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not.” New gods that came newly up. The white Jesus is a new god; he was created during the Renaissance. Islam is a new god, created around 600 AD, after Christ. Those are the new gods our people went after, gods our fathers never feared.

So when a Christ appears in the sky, or they say he is in the desert or in the secret chambers, it is another new god come newly up, and to worship it is to sacrifice unto devils, not to God.

precepts.text: The Most High divided the nations and separated the sons of Adam by the number of the children of Israel; Jacob is His portion.
precepts.point: After Babel the Most High sent every family back to where it was supposed to be: Ham to his place, Shem to his, Japheth to his.

note.label: Genesis 11: Babel and the Separation of the Nations

precepts.why:
The people being one at Babel was not going to produce righteousness. Nothing would be restrained from what they imagined to do, and it would be evil, so the Most High confounded their language and scattered them. There has never been a doctrine of all nations holding hands as one in the scriptures.

“Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee. When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.”

The Most High divided the nations their inheritance and separated the sons of Adam, setting the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel; Jacob is his portion. After Babel he sent every family back to where it was supposed to be: Ham to his place, Shem to his, Japheth to his.

precepts.text: A very froward generation, children in whom is no faith; that is the record over Israel.
precepts.point: In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
The Lord had done miracle after miracle before their eyes and brought them out with an high hand, yet at the first sight of the Egyptians marching “they were sore afraid”, and said he had taken them away “to die in the wilderness”. At the first sign of danger Israel lost all faith.

That is the record over Israel: “I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” Our people have always been a rebellious people of little faith, a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. What they said at the sea is what the Lord said of them.

precepts.text: The Most High planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed, and thou art turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine.
precepts.point: They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: the Most High planted us a noble vine, and we became a degenerate plant. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us; we are a perverse and crooked generation.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
The song gives the Most High his praise first: “He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.” Then it turns to what happens when Israel corrupts themselves: “They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: they are a perverse and crooked generation.”

Jeremiah shows the corruption: “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Most High planted us a noble vine, wholly a right seed, and we became the degenerate plant of a strange vine. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us. His work was perfect; the corruption is ours, a perverse and crooked generation grown from a noble vine.

precepts.text: He was Israel's Savior and carried them all the days of old, but they rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit, therefore he was turned to be their enemy.
precepts.point: How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise?” This is how you repay the magnificent Lord that delivered you, that destroyed whole nations just so you could inherit their land? “is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?” Isaiah recounts what there was to repay: “I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel”.

“For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour. In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.” Whenever he saw us going through atrocities he suffered with us. In his love and in his pity he redeemed us, and carried us all the days of old.

How did we repay all that kindness? “But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.” The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we requited him with rebellion. That is the foolish people and unwise of the song.

precepts.text: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.
precepts.point: How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise?” Stephen answers for every generation of Israel: “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” The fathers rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit, and their children always resist the Holy Ghost, the same way.

That is how the people the Most High bought, made and established requited him: rebellion in every generation, until he was turned to be their enemy.

precepts.text: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers.
precepts.point: Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.” Job says the same: “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Study who we were, see where our fathers went wrong, and do not do the same thing.

Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Did you know the many generations of your forefathers? Somebody had to show you. When we suffer persecution and trials we can go to the scriptures and see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers. That is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves: enquiring of the former age, searching out the fathers.

precepts.text: We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.
precepts.point: Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.” The psalm shows it done: “We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.” The knowledge of who we are and what the Most High did for us is passed down by the fathers telling it.

Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Somebody had to show you. The men teaching on the corners and bringing out these prophecies and breakdowns are the ones Moses said would teach you these things: ask thy father, and he will shew thee. Through them we have heard with our ears what work the Most High did in the times of old.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
precepts.point: Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans Paul quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

That is “Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations” in the mouth of an apostle. We go to the scriptures, see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers, see where they went wrong, and take patience, comfort and hope from it. That is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves.

precepts.text: In the division of the nations he set a ruler over every people, but Israel is the Lord's portion.
precepts.point: For the Lord's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. In the division of the nations he set a ruler over every people, but Israel he kept for himself: that is my inheritance, that is my portion.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.” You thought God wants everybody to just come together and hold hands? The God of this Bible has been a God of division from day one. He separated the sons of Adam according to where he had to place the children of Israel, meaning this world revolves around Israel.

Ecclesiasticus shows the division: “For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Israel is the Lord’s portion”. Every people got a ruler set over them, but Israel he kept for himself. That is “the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance”: that is my inheritance, that is my portion.

precepts.text: Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon, for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
precepts.point: He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye: the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye.” The same people the world counted as three fifths of a man are the apple of the Most High's eye. Zechariah shows who that people is: “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord. Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.”

Who was held captive in the land of the north, in North America, but the so-called blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans? We are Zion, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon, and we must deliver ourselves from the ways we were taught there.

“For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” Israel is still the apple of his eye, and the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns.

precepts.text: Edom is remembered against the day of Jerusalem, and the daughter of Babylon is to be destroyed; this shows who Zion dwells with.
precepts.point: He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye: the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
Zion dwells with the daughter of Babylon, and the psalm shows who that is: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof. O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.” Edom is remembered against the day of Jerusalem, and the daughter of Babylon is to be destroyed and rewarded as she served us.

That is the payback for touching the apple of his eye. The people the Most High kept as the apple of his eye were held captive in the land of the north with the daughter of Babylon, and the nations that spoiled them, Edom among them, will be rewarded as they served us when Christ returns.

precepts.text: Lest when thou hast eaten and art full and all thou hast is multiplied, thine heart be lifted up and thou forget the Lord thy God.
precepts.point: With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God; we get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”. Jeshurun is Israel. Waxing fat is not about being overweight; Deuteronomy 8 explains it: “Lest when thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and dwelt therein; And when thy herds and thy flocks multiply, and thy silver and thy gold is multiplied, and all that thou hast is multiplied; Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage”.

That is what it means to wax fat, grow thick and be covered with fatness: full, housed, herds and silver and gold multiplied, and the heart lifted up. With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God. We get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High. That is how Israel “forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation”: forgetting the one who brought us out of the house of bondage.

precepts.text: They all drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.” Who is that Rock? Paul says of Israel in the wilderness that they “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

Christ did not begin two thousand years after Moses. He was with Israel in the wilderness, the spiritual Rock that followed them, the Rock that begat us. And when it comes to the Rock that created us, we are unmindful.

precepts.text: David says the Lord is my rock, and then the God of my rock; in him will I trust.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
David distinguishes two: “The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; The God of my rock; in him will I trust”. There is the Lord my rock, and there is the God of my rock. You have our Rock, which is Christ, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

David understood that difference before anybody else. The Rock that begat Israel, the one we are unmindful of, is Christ, and above him is his God.

precepts.text: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.” David heard the Lord speak unto his Lord: the Father speaking, and the Son seated at his right hand. It is the same distinction David makes between the Lord my rock and the God of my rock.

David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. The Rock that begat Israel is Christ, and the God of that Rock is the Father who set him at his right hand.

precepts.text: The head of every man is Christ, and the head of Christ is God.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
Paul lays out the order David saw: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” The head of Christ is God. That is why David could say the Lord is my rock and then the God of my rock, and the Lord said unto my Lord.

So the Rock that begat thee is Christ, the spiritual Rock that followed Israel in the wilderness, and over that Rock is his head, the Father. Of the Rock we have been unmindful, and God that formed us we have forgotten.

precepts.text: Christ called the froward, faithless generation of his day serpents and a generation of vipers.
precepts.point: The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters. And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” This goes especially into Judah, the southern kingdom. When Christ was on the scene, the scribes and Pharisees rejected him; they were very froward and had no faith that he was the Son of God.

Christ called them what the song calls them: “Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?” A very froward generation, children in whom is no faith, a generation of vipers: the same people.

precepts.text: Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim, head of the northern kingdom, be broken, that it be not a people.
precepts.point: The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people”. Some close the book right there and say the Most High welcomed all the other nations in place of Israel. No: the ones which are not a people are also Israel.

Isaiah says who: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” Ephraim, the head of the northern kingdom, was broken so that it be not a people. The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. Those which are not a people are our own brothers and sisters, broken off for a dispensation of time.

precepts.text: Ye are not my people; yet in the place where that was said, it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
Hosea says it of the northern kingdom: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” There are those which are not a people. “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

That is how the Most High moves Judah to jealousy with those which are not a people, and provokes them to anger with a foolish nation. The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, it provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? The nation which was not a people was our own brothers and sisters, broken off for a dispensation of time, and now called the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: He shall assemble the outcasts of Israel and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: The nations we were scattered to took counsel together: come, let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. Divide them, teach them they are not who they really are: if I get them to take pride in being called anything but Israel, they will never remember. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, but the remembrance has not completely ceased.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. What corners? Isaiah shows: “he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah are gathered from the four corners of the earth, so the scattering was worldwide.

What nation of people has been scattered throughout the four corners of the earth by slave trades, the transatlantic, the sub-Saharan, the silk road? The so-called blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans. This never happened to the people claiming our heritage; it is further proof of who the children of Israel are.

precepts.text: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.
precepts.point: The nations we were scattered to took counsel together: come, let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. Divide them, teach them they are not who they really are: if I get them to take pride in being called anything but Israel, they will never remember. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, but the remembrance has not completely ceased.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The nations we were scattered to took counsel together to do just that: “They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.”

Divide them, teach them they are not who they really are: if I get them to take pride in being called anything but Israel, they will never remember. That is the crafty counsel of the nations against the name of Israel. But the remembrance has not completely ceased.

precepts.text: They turned their back unto the Most High, but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us; let the gods they made save them, for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods.
precepts.point: Jeremiah says our people say to a stock, Thou art my father, and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth; but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us. Where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? Let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods. That is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities; that is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted, Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, and drank the wine of their drink offerings? let them rise up and help you, and be your protection.” Now that you are being shot down in the street, locked in cages, where are the idols and the saints you prayed to? Let them rise up and help you.

Jeremiah says the same of our people: “Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth: for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.” We turned our back to the Most High and our face to a stock and a stone, and when the trouble comes we cry to him, arise and save us. His answer: “But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah.”

According to the number of thy cities are thy gods: that is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities. That is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day. The Most High had to let it play out over a span of time, allowing enemies to afflict us, so we would see that the gods we went off to worship were not real gods, because they could not help when the Lord sent the enemy against us.

precepts.text: The innocent and righteous blood crieth unto the Most High, and he saith, I will surely avenge them.
precepts.point: This is fulfilled in the destruction of Babylon: rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets, for God hath avenged you on her. Babylon the great in this teaching is the United States of America; that is where the Lord makes his arrows drunk with blood, the vengeance promised for all the wrong these nations have done unto us.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries”. Whose blood? Read through the Bible: Christ put to death, James put to death, Peter put to death, and since the Bible was written more prophets have lost their lives for the truth, and it will continue.

Ezra hears the Most High's answer to that blood: “I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickedness, which they profanely commit, neither will I suffer them in those things, in which they wickedly exercise themselves: behold, the innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me, and the souls of the just complain continually.” The souls of the just keep asking when he will act. “And therefore, saith the Lord, I will surely avenge them, and receive unto me all the innocent blood from among them.” That is the avenging of the blood of his servants that the song promises.

precepts.text: Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.
precepts.point: This is fulfilled in the destruction of Babylon: rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets, for God hath avenged you on her. Babylon the great in this teaching is the United States of America; that is where the Lord makes his arrows drunk with blood, the vengeance promised for all the wrong these nations have done unto us.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
The vengeance of the song is fulfilled in the destruction of Babylon: “Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.” The holy apostles and prophets whose blood was shed, Christ, James, Peter and the rest, are avenged on Babylon, and heaven is told to rejoice, just as the song says “Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants”.

Babylon the great in this teaching is the United States of America. That is where the Lord makes his arrows drunk with blood, the vengeance promised for all the wrong these nations have done unto us, and after it he “will be merciful unto his land, and to his people.”

precepts.text: They angered him at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes, because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.
precepts.point: Thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
That selfsame day the Most High tells Moses to get up into mount Nebo, behold the land of Canaan, and die in the mount as Aaron died in mount Hor, “Because ye trespassed against me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah–Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin; because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel.” The account is in Numbers 20, and the psalm tells how it went: “They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes: Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.”

The people angered Moses at the waters of strife, complaining and provoking him after all they had already seen, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes. They provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips: Hear now, ye rebels; and he smote the rock twice instead of speaking to it, the Rock we read about earlier in this chapter. That is how he sanctified not the Most High in the midst of the children of Israel.

So the sentence stands: “Yet thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither unto the land which I give the children of Israel.”

precepts.text: Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.
precepts.point: This is why we must know our history. The king of Ammon could have pulled that on somebody ignorant and been given the land; Jephthah said no, that is not what happened, the book of Numbers does not say that. People try to confuse us about the Bible in the street the same way, so prepare yourself to the search of the fathers.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why: “Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.” Jephthah remembered the days of old: Israel coming up from Egypt, walking through the wilderness unto the Red sea and to Kadesh, sending messengers to the king of Edom and to the king of Moab, compassing their lands, pitching on the other side of Arnon, and never coming within the border of Moab. That is the knowledge handed down from the fathers and the elders, and it is what let him answer the king of Ammon. We must know our history the same way, so nobody can pull the wool over our eyes.

precepts.text: See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand. There is no Buddha, there is no Allah, there is no Krishna; all of that is made-up imaginations of men.
precepts.point: The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.”

That is Hannah's word: “The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.” The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.

He says, “there is no god with me.” There is no Buddha, there is no Allah, there is no Krishna; all of that is made-up imaginations of men.

precepts.text: Jeshurun waxed fat and kicked, forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation; that is what Israel did.
precepts.point: The Most High made David's feet like hinds' feet and set him upon high places, and taught his hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms, not bent but broken. He gave David the shield of his salvation and his gentleness made him great; his repentance enlarged his steps so his feet did not slip. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.” That is what Israel did.

David knew where his strength came from: “God is my strength and power: and he maketh my way perfect.” This is what Israel forgot. We waxed fat and kicked, forgot the Most High and where our strength came from, and began to say we are lords ourselves.

But our strength comes from the Most High, who is merciful enough to let us take a breath and blink our eyes every moment.

precepts.text: Jeshurun waxed fat and kicked, forsaking the Most High and provoking Him with strange gods and vanities.
precepts.point: All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

precepts.why:
Moses foretold it: “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”. Israel grew fat, “then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” They “sacrificed unto devils, not to God”, to new gods their fathers never feared.

The Most High says, “they have provoked me to anger with their vanities”. That is the same word spoken over Baasha and Elah his son: all the house of Baasha was destroyed “For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son”, who made Israel to sin, “in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.”

So when Zimri, captain of half his chariots, slew Elah while he was drinking himself drunk in Tirzah, and then left not one male of the house of Baasha, it came “according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet”. It was the Most High answering the provoking of his people.

precepts.text: The Most High moved Israel to jealousy and anger, foretelling their rejection among the nations.
precepts.point: This rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, which resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.”

Israel provoked the Most High with their vanities, and he was very angry and “removed them out of his sight.” He “rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight.” This foretells their rejection among the nations.

That rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, and it resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there.

precepts.text: He is a rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are judgment, a God of truth and without iniquity; all the ways of the Lord are judgment.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever; the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. This whole Bible is the ways of the Lord, the judgments of the Lord, true and righteous altogether; if you want to know what righteousness is you have to learn and follow the Bible.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether.” Moses says: “He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.”

He is a rock, his work is perfect, and all his ways are judgment, a God of truth and without iniquity. This whole Bible is the ways of the Lord, the judgments of the Lord, true and righteous altogether. If you want to know what righteousness is, you have to learn and follow the Bible.

precepts.text: Remember the days of old; ask thy father and he will show thee, thy elders and they will tell thee.
precepts.point: When brothers ask "were you there?" or "how you know what color he was?" the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. We are supposed to search the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.” That is exactly what Moses commanded: “Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.”

When brothers ask were you there, or how you know what color he was, the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. The fathers told how the Most High drove out the heathen with his hand and planted Israel, and that Israel “got not the land in possession by their own sword”, but by his right hand and “the light of thy countenance, because thou hadst a favour unto them.” We are supposed to search the scriptures, where the fathers and elders still tell it.

precepts.text: See now that I, even I, am He, and there is no God with me; I kill and I make alive, I wound and I heal, neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.
precepts.point: There is something we must understand: to the Lord belong the issues of death. That is why you see people get shot many times and still live, or go through things people wonder how they survived. When it is not your time you are not going, and when it is your time you are not staying.

note.label: Psalm 68: Let God Arise

precepts.why:
“He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death.” There is something we must understand: to the Lord belong the issues of death. “See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.”

That is why you see people get shot many times and still live, or go through things people wonder how they survived. When it is not your time, you are not going; and when it is your time, you are not staying. He kills and he makes alive, he wounds and he heals, and none can deliver out of his hand. Blessed be the Lord who daily loadeth us with benefits; as Lamentations 3 says, his mercy is renewed every morning.

precepts.text: They provoked Him to jealousy with strange gods and sacrificed unto devils, and they were unmindful of the Rock that begot them and forgot God that formed them; the Rock is the Lord.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
Israel had to be slain before they remembered that God was their rock. Moses tells how they forgot him: “They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger. They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not. Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.”

They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods and sacrificed unto devils, and they were unmindful of the Rock that begot them and forgot God that formed them. The Rock is the Lord.

That is why he slew them, and that is why, when he did, “they remembered that God was their rock”. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way he wants, until we turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High.

precepts.text: He made him to suck honey out of the rock and oil out of the flinty rock.
precepts.point: He would have fed them with the finest of the wheat and with honey out of the rock He would have satisfied them. The honey out of the rock goes into salvation and the future rest we were meant to have coming out of Egypt into Canaan, the land that became Israel.

note.label: Psalm 81: Open Thy Mouth Wide and I Will Fill It

precepts.why:
If Israel had hearkened, “He should have fed them also with the finest of the wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied thee.” Moses sang of that honey: “He made him ride on the high places of the earth, that he might eat the increase of the fields; and he made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock”.

He made him to suck honey out of the rock and oil out of the flinty rock. The honey out of the rock goes into salvation and the future rest we were meant to have coming out of Egypt into Canaan, the land that became Israel.

Had we walked in his ways, he would soon have subdued our enemies and turned his hand against our adversaries, and the haters of the Lord would have submitted themselves unto him. The honey out of the rock is what that rest would have been.

precepts.text: The Most High scattered us into corners as a curse, but feared the wrath of the enemy lest they should say their hand is high; He knows the heathen are a nation void of counsel.
precepts.point: The Most High knoweth the thoughts of man that they are vanity. He knows our thoughts as His heritage, and He knows the thoughts of the heathen because He created them.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“The Lord knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are vanity.” He knows our thoughts as his heritage, and he knows the thoughts of the heathen because he created them. Moses shows him weighing both: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men: Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this.”

The Most High scattered us into corners as a curse, but he feared the wrath of the enemy, lest they should say their hand is high and the Lord has not done all this. He knows what the heathen would think. “For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them.” He knows the heathen are a nation void of counsel.

That is why the psalm says “Understand, ye brutish among the people: and ye fools, when will ye be wise?” He that planted the ear shall hear and he that formed the eye shall see, and he that teaches man knowledge knows the vain thoughts of the nations who think their own hand did this to Israel.

precepts.text: Being scattered ties into loving your neighbor as yourself; going into the Passover season we must purge out the old leaven of malice and hatred and get our spirits right.
precepts.point: Zedekiah and his princes He will give into the hand of Babylon's army, which He will cause to return, take, and burn the city, and make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
The Lord will cause the king of Babylon's army to return, take the city, burn it with fire, and make the cities of Judah a desolation without an inhabitant. He had said it in the song of Moses: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”.

Being scattered ties into loving your neighbor as yourself. Judah was scattered into corners for bringing their brothers back into bondage after proclaiming them free.
